title: Fully dynamic linear programming with outliers
formal: Can fully dynamic planar linear programming with at most k violated halfplanes be maintained with (k+1)^{O(1)} polylogarithmic amortized update time and near-linear-plus-polynomial-in-k space?
definitions:
Fix integer k≥0 and nonzero objective vector c∈R². Maintain n labeled closed halfplanes H_i={x∈R²:a_i·x≤b_i}, with a_i≠0, under arbitrary online insertions and deletions. A point is feasible if it lies outside at most k active halfplanes; boundary points satisfy a constraint. A query must return infeasible if no such point exists, unbounded if c·x is unbounded below on feasible points, and otherwise an exact minimizer and its objective value. Any minimizer is acceptable. The feasible region is a finite union of closed polyhedra, so finite optima are attained. When n≤k the unconstrained objective is unbounded.

Use a real-RAM with exact +,−,×,division by nonzero scalars, comparisons and memory access at unit cost, but no floor or arbitrary real-to-bit extraction. A randomized Las Vegas structure may be used: outputs are always correct and time bounds are in expectation for every fixed oblivious update/query sequence. Start empty with poly(k+1) initialization. For absolute c0,d require space O(n log^{c0}(n+2)+(k+1)^d), expected amortized update time O((k+1)^d log^{c0}(n+2)), and expected query time bounded by the same expression; current n, or the larger of the sizes before and after an update, controls these bounds. No future deletion times are supplied.
